sections.h2: How Does ERPNext Run a Factory?
sections.intro: ERPNext connects every step from sales order to dispatch. A sales order creates a production plan, the plan raises work orders and material requests, the shop floor records progress, and finished goods move to stock with their real cost. Setting up ERPNext for manufacturing usually takes 10–16 weeks for a single plant. The ERPNext manufacturing module covers:
rows: Raw materials, sub-assemblies, operations and scrap for each product
What to make, when, and what materials to buy
Instructions for each batch, with materials issued from stock
Job cards for each operation, with time and quantity
Inspection checks on incoming, in-process and finished goods
Material, labour and overhead cost per unit
sections.note: Because accounts, stock and buying live in the same system, ERPNext for manufacturers removes the gap between what the factory makes and what the books show.

outro.text: If three or more apply, ERPNext for manufacturing usually pays for itself through less waste, fewer stock-outs and faster month-end closing.

sections.h2: Bills of Materials and Production Planning

paragraphs.text: A good bill of materials is the base of everything. We set up single-level and multi-level BOMs, with alternate materials, operations, workstations and expected scrap. When a product changes, the new version is tracked so past costs stay correct.

ERPNext production planning turns sales orders and forecasts into a plan. It checks stock on hand, shows what is short and raises material requests for purchasing. Planners see what to make this week, which work orders are late and which materials will run out. Reorder levels and lead times for each raw material can be set, so purchasing gets an early warning instead of a last-minute rush order.
ERPNext for manufacturing works for both make-to-order and make-to-stock businesses, and for mixed models where standard items are stocked and special items are built to order.
ERPNext work order management gives each batch a clear set of instructions and a materials list. Stores issue materials against the work order, so stock records stay accurate.

ERPNext shop floor management uses job cards for each operation. Operators or supervisors record time and quantity on a tablet or desktop, and managers see progress live. This ERPNext production tracking shows where each order is, which workstation is busy and where delays build up.
For work sent to outside job workers, ERPNext tracks materials sent out, finished goods received and job-work charges, so nothing goes missing between your plant and theirs.

Quality checks can be set at goods receipt, between operations and before dispatch. Failed items are held, so they cannot be sold or used by mistake. Each check records who inspected, what was measured and why an item passed or failed, which helps with customer audits and ISO records.

Costing is where many factories finally see the truth. With ERPNext for manufacturing, each finished unit carries its real material, labour and overhead cost, so you can compare actual cost with your selling price. Our ERPNext manufacturing reports then show margin by product, scrap by operation, late orders and stock ageing.
ERPNext inventory for manufacturing keeps raw materials, work in progress and finished goods in separate warehouses, with batch and serial numbers where you need them.

sections.h2: Which Manufacturers Is ERPNext Right For?
rows: Food, chemicals, cosmetics, batches with expiry
Job-based work, quotations per job, project costing
sections.note:
ERPNext for discrete manufacturing relies on multi-level BOMs and serial numbers. ERPNext for process manufacturing relies on batches, expiry dates and yield tracking. We set up whichever fits, or both.

Common sectors we set up include ERPNext for food manufacturers, ERPNext for furniture manufacturers and ERPNext for packaging manufacturers. Each needs different reports and checks, so we configure ERPNext for manufacturing around your products, not a generic template.

paragraphs.text: ERPNext for engineering companies combines manufacturing with project work. Each job gets its own quotation, BOM, work orders, purchases and timesheets, so you can see profit per job before you invoice. This suits fabrication shops, machine builders and panel makers that rarely make the same thing twice. Estimators can copy a past job as a starting point, so quotations for similar work take minutes instead of hours.

items.q: Is ERPNext good for small factories?
items.a: Yes. ERPNext manufacturing software has no licence fee per user, so small factories can start with core features and add shop-floor tracking later. Many go live in 10–12 weeks.

items.q: How long does it take to set up ERPNext in a factory?
items.a: A single plant with one product line usually goes live in 10–12 weeks. Multi-plant groups or complex BOMs take 14–20 weeks. Rolling out ERPNext for manufacturing one line at a time keeps production running throughout.

items.q: Do operators need computers on the shop floor?
items.a: Not necessarily. Supervisors can update job cards on a tablet or phone, or record progress at the end of each shift from a desktop.

items.q: Can it work for food and batch production?
items.a: Yes. ERPNext for factories making food or chemicals uses batch numbers, expiry dates, yield tracking and quality checks, so every batch can be traced back to its raw materials.
